---
name: morning-read
description: Use when a seller hands over a day's calendar, an open-deal ledger and outstanding tasks, and wants a morning briefing. Return the finished Daily Briefing page. Two ledger rows can look identical and mean opposite things — quiet because the buyer asked for room is not quiet because nobody worked it. A documented wait that has run out is not a wait, and a window that opens today is often the most valuable move. Verbal-plus-paper already in motion is a final-stage carveout; an expired link or an unsent artifact on settled terms is a five-minute unblock. Automatic logs are not contact. A deal on today's calendar never takes an outbound slot. Irreversible damage outranks size. How many deals need a move is whatever the evidence shows — three on a well-run book is a finding, ten or eleven on a large book in motion is honest — never pad, never trim to look disciplined. Seller prose outranks the export. Stale, contradictory, machine-stamped or missing fields are named, not guessed. Finish the briefing first; anything outside it is a footnote, not a reason to shrink the page.
---

# The morning read

<!-- Un commercial, un matin. Choisir les affaires où un geste aujourd'hui change
l'issue, dire exactement quel geste, et être honnête sur le reste pour que le
livre puisse être ignoré en confiance. -->

Produce the finished page and nothing else — no preamble, no restated ledger, no account of
the method. Treat what was handed over as the entire world. Every name, role, date and figure
on the page comes from it. An invented row is worse than a missing one, because it will be
acted on. Never reuse deal names from memory or from any example; if a name is not on the
page you were handed, it does not exist.
<!-- Les colonnes sont un export. Les phrases autour — paragraphe du haut, aparté
en bas, avertissement de la première ligne — sont une personne qui dit ce qu'elle
sait, et c'est là que se joue le jugement du matin. Si la prose contredit le
tableau, croire la personne, dire la date utilisée, et mettre la ligne dans
Needs Record Update plutôt que raisonner sur un chiffre faux. Un renseignement
de seconde main affine une inquiétude déjà dans le dossier ; jamais le traiter
comme un fait. Les jours ouvrés ne s'arrêtent pas pour les congés. Ne pas
rétrograder tout le livre parce que le commercial a une excuse. -->
## Reading before judging

The columns are an export. The sentences around them — the paragraph above, the aside at the
foot, the heads-up in the first line — are a person telling you what they know, and that is
usually where the morning's real judgement sits: a champion who named the week they would be
back, a conversation the record has not caught up with, a date the seller knows is wrong, a
stretch of time they were away, a warning that today is unusual. Where the prose disagrees
with the table, believe the person, say which date you judged from, and put the row in
Needs Record Update rather than reasoning from a number known to be false. Where the report
is second-hand (a conference rumour, a colleague's aside), let it sharpen a concern the
record already carries; never print it as confirmed fact.

Business days do not pause for PTO. If the seller was away, the gap the buyer experienced
is still the gap. Do not demote a book because the seller has an excuse.
## Where a move is worth making

<!-- Un geste vaut la peine s'il réduit aujourd'hui le risque que l'affaire
tourne mal, ou s'il achète une information qui justifie l'interruption.
Quatre situations en ont l'air et n'en sont pas : les filtrer avant tout
classement, puis vérifier la date contre aujourd'hui. -->

A move is worth making when doing it today measurably lowers the chance the deal ends badly,
or buys information worth the interruption. In practice that is: no genuine human contact in
about ten business days; a stage held past the point it normally turns over; a date close
enough that something unresolved threatens it; something the seller owes that a named person
is waiting on; a structural break — the champion gone, the sponsor unconfirmed, a competitor
arriving late, a two-vendor decision due this week; or a field missing on a deal closing soon,
where the call that fills the gap is itself the move.

Four situations look like all of that and are not. Screen them out before anything is ranked,
so nothing can be argued back in by its size. Then check the date against today, every time.

**A documented wait is the plan working.**
<!-- Attente documentée = le plan fonctionne. Période d'évaluation demandée par
le client, contact absent jusqu'à une date nommée, consigne de ne pas appeler,
champion en sabbatique : le silence est convenu. Une attente expirée n'en est
plus une ; une fenêtre qui s'ouvre ce matin est souvent le geste le plus
précieux. Une consigne sans date reste une consigne. « Ils comparent des
vendeurs, décision la semaine prochaine » n'est pas une attente — c'est une
fenêtre qui se ferme, donc un geste. -->
An evaluation period the customer asked for, a
contact away until a named date, an instruction not to make contact, a champion on a
documented sabbatical — the quiet is agreed, however long it has run, and arriving early is
the error. A wait that has run out is not a wait, and a window opening this morning is often
the most valuable thing on the page. Where a period is given rather than a day, work out
where it ends. An open-ended instruction is still an instruction. "They are comparing vendors
with a decision next week" is not a wait — it is a closing window and it earns a move.

**Paper in motion is not paper owed.**
<!-- Papier en cours ≠ papier dû. Accord verbal ET contrats/juridique déjà en
mouvement = exception de stade final : surveiller, ne pas brûler un créneau
sortant. Deux exceptions qui passent devant : (1) termes d'accord mais artefact
à envoyer manquant, expiré ou jamais émis — cinq minutes, ça bat une plus grosse
affaire qui attend. (2) verbal reçu mais MSA encore dû avec clôture dans la
semaine — demander la date de retour aujourd'hui. Un document déjà sur un bureau
nommé : une seule demande de date de retour. Le silence au-delà du test de
contact bat une note qui dit encore « chez le juridique ». -->
Verbal received *and* contracts or legal drafting
already under way (their side or a live redline) is a final-stage carveout: monitor it, do
not spend an outbound slot on it, whatever the close date says. Two exceptions, and they
lead when they appear. (1) Terms are agreed but the artifact the seller must send is missing,
expired, or never issued — a fresh link, a template, an order form. Five minutes, and it
outranks a larger deal that is merely waiting. (2) Verbal received but the MSA or paper is
still outstanding with a close inside a week — it has not entered the carveout yet; ask for
the return date today. A document already on a named desk (markup outstanding, signature
pending) earns exactly one request for when it returns, once the date is close enough to
matter. Silence past the contact test beats a note that still says "with legal."

**A booked conversation is coverage, not a move.**
<!-- Un rendez-vous déjà posé couvre l'affaire : jamais dans Top 3 Actions,
seulement Meeting Prep. Si le même deal déclenche aussi un test d'écart de
contact, le dire dans la ligne de meeting, une fois — pas d'outbound inventé,
pas de doublon Tier A. Les 1:1 internes et revues de forecast : une clause,
marqués internal. -->
A deal the seller is meeting today never
appears in Top 3 Actions. It appears under Meeting Prep. If that same deal independently
trips a contact or close-date test, say so *inside* the meeting line (the meeting is today's
coverage) — do not also invent an outbound for it, and do not duplicate it as a second Tier A
story. Internal 1:1s and forecast reviews get a clause and are marked internal.

**A system did not talk to anyone.**
<!-- Un journal automatique n'est pas un contact. Compter les jours ouvrés depuis
le dernier échange humain, et écrire cette date. Entre deux silences, la date
humaine la plus ancienne est la plus froide. -->
Automatic logs, sequence sends, renewal notices, opened
mail, marketing workflows — none are contact. Find the last time a person engaged, write that
date on the page, and count business days from it. Between two quiet deals the earlier human
date is the colder one.

Then rank what survives on two axes read together, not in sequence.

**What is exposed, and how soon.**
<!-- Exposition = argent en jeu × temps restant. Une grosse affaire qui clôture
dans la période avec quelque chose d'ouvert reste dans les trois, sauf écran
ci-dessus. Ne jamais l'écarter pour quelque chose de plus petit qui a seulement
l'air plus occupé. -->
Money at risk and time remaining are one quantity. A large
deal closing inside the current period with anything still unresolved belongs among the three
unless a screen above covers it. Never leave that close out in favour of something smaller
that merely looks busier.

**What cannot be recovered.**
<!-- Irreversible : champion parti sans successeur, évaluation qui tranche cette
semaine, concurrent tardif, blocage créé par le commercial sur des termes déjà
arrêtés, grosse affaire noire depuis des semaines. Ça bat une plus grosse
affaire qui attend. Le déblocage de cinq minutes sur termes d'accord passe
devant. -->
A champion gone with no successor, an evaluation deciding this
week, a competitor arriving late, a blocker the seller created on terms already settled, a
dark high-value deal whose last human contact is weeks old. These outrank a larger deal that
is merely waiting. The five-minute unblock on settled terms leads outright.

Where the two axes disagree, Top 3 carries both: the period's largest unresolved close, the
sharpest irreversible case, then whichever remainder has the most of either. Size alone never
leads and size is never last.
## How many is the right number

<!-- C'est là que les matins se trompent, et toujours dans le même sens.
Tier A = les affaires qui ont gagné un geste ET qui ne sont pas déjà couvertes
par le calendrier du jour. Top 3 Actions n'est que le front de cet ensemble,
sortant uniquement. Le chiffre en tête est la taille de Tier A, pas un quota. -->

This is where most mornings go wrong, and they go wrong in one direction.

Tier A is the set of deals that earned a move *and are not already covered by today's
calendar*. Top 3 Actions is only the front of that set, outbound only. The count named at
the top is the size of Tier A (Top 3 plus Other), not a quota.

- A well-run book that earns three moves: print three, say the pipeline is healthy, and write
  "no additional Tier A" rather than hunting for a fourth.
  <!-- Livre sain à trois gestes : imprimer trois, dire que le pipeline est sain. -->
- A well-run book that earns one or two: print one or two. Do not fill the third seat with
  lesser-tier work, a task, or a hold you rebranded as proactive.
  <!-- Un ou deux : ne pas remplir le troisième siège. -->
- A large book genuinely in motion can put ten or eleven in Tier A. Print three at the front
  and the rest under Tier A — Other. Do not demote to 3–8 to look disciplined.
  <!-- Gros livre en mouvement : 10–11 en Tier A est honnête. -->
- A deal touched inside the contact test whose note says what happens next is progressing.
  A visible close date does not promote it and neither does a large figure.
- Routine work the seller will do anyway — a post-demo summary, notes from yesterday — is a
  task. Mention it as admin, never as Top 3.

Name the deals that met a test on their face and were left alone anyway, with the clause that
left them (eval until D, do-not-contact, sabbatical, paper already in motion). The reader
should see reasoning, not a gap.
## What a move has to say

<!-- Une affaire, un acte, une personne, une demande, le fait qui fait que c'est
aujourd'hui. L'acte doit coller à la raison du blocage. -->

One deal, one act, one person, one ask, the one fact that makes it today. The act has to fit
why the deal is stuck.

- Silence: one question answerable in a word — still live, budget still there, who owns it
  now. Do not add a qualification probe on top. Give a cheap way back.
  <!-- Silence : une question à un mot. Pas de sonde de qualification en plus. -->
- Champion gone: call the replacement if one is named; if none is named, the ask is who owns
  the budget line now. Do not send them hunting through a network as the primary act.
  <!-- Champion parti : appeler le remplaçant nommé ; sinon, qui tient la ligne budgétaire. -->
- Seller owes a thing: send the thing, do not write about sending it.
- Paper on a desk: ask for the date it returns, not for "progress."
  <!-- Papier sur un bureau : demander la date de retour, pas « l'avancement ». -->
- Missing next-step on a near close: the call is the triage *and* the repair. Put the same
  deal in Needs Record Update to be filled after the call. Do not invent a status, and do not
  drop the deal because a field is blank.
- Channel: a call when the deal is large, silent, or close; writing when the artifact *is*
  the point. Never *follow up*, *touch base*, *check in*.
## The page

Use this skeleton. Do not invent other section titles (no "Morning Read", no parallel tier
labels). Omit a section that has nothing in it rather than padding it.

```
# Daily Briefing — <Weekday, Month D>
<!-- Ligne en italique seulement si un meeting client commence dans l'heure. -->
[one italic line, only when a customer meeting starts inside the hour: which meeting,
 how long there is, and to read its preparation first]

## Pipeline Health
  <!-- Une ou deux phrases. Valeur et nombre seulement si chaque chiffre se
  vérifie en additionnant les montants imprimés et en recomptant les lignes
  ouvertes. Combien de Tier A aujourd'hui. L'exposition qui domine. Livre
  calme : dire qu'il est sain. Livre lourd : dire ce qui concentre le compte.
  Jamais un million arrondi que l'on n'a pas additionné. -->
  One or two sentences. Open value and count only where every figure can be checked by
  adding the printed amounts and recounting the open rows. How many are Tier A today.
  The one exposure that dominates. On a quiet book, say it is healthy. On a heavy book,
  say what concentrates the count. Never a round million you did not add up.

## Top 3 Actions
  <!-- Au plus trois. Sortant uniquement — rien du calendrier du jour. Une
  phrase : affaire, acte, personne, demande, moment, raison. Moins de trois
  ont gagné un geste : imprimer moins. Ne jamais remplir. -->
  At most three. Outbound only — nothing on today's calendar. One sentence each:
  deal, act, person, ask, timing, reason. If fewer than three earned a move, print
  fewer. Never pad.

## Meeting Prep
  <!-- Chaque conversation posée, ordre chronologique. Qui est dans la pièce et
  ce qu'ils contrôlent, depuis quand un humain a parlé, les deux points à
  tenir. Internes marqués. Un meeting qui déclenche aussi un écart de contact :
  le dire ici, une fois. -->
  Every booked conversation in time order. Who is in the room and what they control,
  how long since a person last engaged, and the two specifics to hold. Internal items
  marked as such. If a meeting deal also trips a contact-gap test, say it here, once.

## Tier A — Other Deals Needing Action Today
  <!-- Le reste de Tier A, une clause, avec l'acte. Si Top 3 est déjà l'ensemble,
  une ligne — ne pas réimprimer les trois. -->
  The rest of Tier A, one clause each, with its act. If Top 3 already is the whole
  set, write that in one line — do not reprint the three.

## Tier B — Monitor
  <!-- Holds et affaires qui avancent, groupés par motif et comptés. Détailler
  seulement les holds nommés. Pas de roman de statut pour chaque ligne calme. -->
  Holds and progressing deals, grouped by reason and counted. Spell out only named
  holds (eval, do-not-contact, sabbatical, paper-in-motion carveout). Do not write a
  status novel for every quiet row.

## Needs Record Update
  <!-- Un fragment par ligne défectueuse : ce qui cloche, la date réellement
  utilisée, ce qui réparerait. Les erreurs de journal déjà avouées vont ici,
  pas dans Top 3. -->
  One fragment per defective row: what is wrong, which date you actually judged from,
  and what would repair it. Logging errors the seller already confessed belong here,
  not in Top 3.
```

Never print the tests or the ranking method. The page carries verdicts. If the seller asked
for something that is not this briefing (a forecast, a quarterly model, a rewrite in another
format), finish the six sections first, then decline in a single footnote. Do not skip or
shrink the briefing to make the decline.
<!-- Terminer les six sections d'abord ; décliner hors-périmètre en une note de
bas de page. Ne pas raccourcir le briefing pour faire le refus. -->
## What the page must fit inside

Write to about 380 words, never more than 450. Spend words on Top 3 and Meeting Prep first.
Everything after that is fragments. As the day gets larger, Tier B groups harder, never
longer. A page that stops mid-sentence has failed.
<!-- Environ 380 mots, jamais plus de 450. D'abord Top 3 et Meeting Prep.
Ensuite des fragments. Un page coupée en milieu de phrase a échoué. -->

A line earns its words by saying something the ledger does not: what to do, why now, or why
not. Do not restate a field the seller is already looking at. Do not duplicate a meeting deal
under Tier A after Meeting Prep already covered it.

Every figure is one you have actually worked out. Count the open rows and count them again.
Add amounts only where every open row carries one you can read. Keep currencies apart. Where
the total cannot be checked, give the count and the exposure that matters instead of a sum —
a number that is close is worse than no number. A ledger handed over once is a photograph:
say nothing about what moved since yesterday unless yesterday is on the page too.
<!-- Chaque chiffre doit survivre à un recomptage. Un total approximatif est
pire que pas de total. Le grand livre est une photo, pas un film. -->
## Before it goes

- Every deal in the ledger is accounted for once: Top 3, Meeting Prep, Tier A Other, Tier B,
  or Needs Record Update.
- Top 3 is outbound and none of it is on the calendar.
- Every booked conversation has a line.
- The top line's figures would survive a recount.
- Named holds are visible, with the clause that left them out of Tier A.
- No deal name appears that was not on the page you were handed.
- Out-of-scope asks, if any, are a footnote under a complete briefing.
- The page ends on a finished sentence.
<!-- Contrôle final : chaque affaire une fois ; Top 3 sans calendrier ; meetings
couverts ; totaux vérifiables ; holds nommés visibles ; aucun nom inventé ;
hors-périmètre en note ; phrase de fin complète. -->

# Daily Briefing — Tuesday, October 8

*Discovery call with Harmon Medical Devices at 9:00 AM (60 min); read Meeting Prep first.*

## Pipeline Health

Open pipeline totals $1,363K across 12 deals. You are at 61% of quarterly quota with 23 days remaining in the period. Thornfield Logistics ($310K, Oct 14 close) and Nightfall Insurance ($200K, Oct 18 close) are the two largest exposures inside the close window, both in negotiation with unresolved terms. Bluewater Shipping ($130K, Oct 11) is verbal with contracts in motion — monitor only. The book is active but concentrated: three deals account for $640K of the near-term close risk, and two of them need moves today.

## Top 3 Actions

1. **Nightfall Insurance** — Send revised payment terms proposal to procurement today. They flagged this as the blocker; the artifact is the move. Confirm receipt once sent.

2. **Redwood Partners** — Call the main contact to identify who owns the budget line now that the champion has left. Do not ask them to hunt for a replacement; ask who holds the decision. This is urgent per your manager and the deal is stalled (last activity Sep 12, 23 business days).

3. **Thornfield Logistics** — Prep the legal call agenda for 4:00 PM. Confirm with Marcus Webb and Priya Nair that you have their redlines and know which terms are still open. This call is your coverage; use it to surface any remaining gaps before close (Oct 14).

---
name: morning-read
description: Use when a seller hands over a day's calendar, an open-deal ledger and outstanding tasks, and wants a morning briefing. Return the finished Daily Briefing page. Two ledger rows can look identical and mean opposite things — quiet because the buyer asked for room is not quiet because nobody worked it. A documented wait that has run out is not a wait, and a window that opens today is often the most valuable move. Verbal-plus-paper already in motion is a final-stage carveout; an expired link or an unsent artifact on settled terms is a five-minute unblock. Automatic logs are not contact. A deal on today's calendar never takes an outbound slot. Irreversible damage outranks size. How many deals need a move is whatever the evidence shows — three on a well-run book is a finding, ten or eleven on a large book in motion is honest — never pad, never trim to look disciplined. Seller prose outranks the export. Stale, contradictory, machine-stamped or missing fields are named, not guessed. Finish the briefing first; anything outside it is a footnote, not a reason to shrink the page.
---

# The morning read

<!-- Un commercial, un matin. Choisir les affaires où un geste aujourd'hui change
l'issue, dire exactement quel geste, et être honnête sur le reste pour que le
livre puisse être ignoré en confiance. -->

Produce the finished page and nothing else — no preamble, no restated ledger, no account of
the method. Treat what was handed over as the entire world. Every name, role, date and figure
on the page comes from it. An invented row is worse than a missing one, because it will be
acted on. Never reuse deal names from memory or from any example; if a name is not on the
page you were handed, it does not exist.
<!-- Les colonnes sont un export. Les phrases autour — paragraphe du haut, aparté
en bas, avertissement de la première ligne — sont une personne qui dit ce qu'elle
sait, et c'est là que se joue le jugement du matin. Si la prose contredit le
tableau, croire la personne, dire la date utilisée, et mettre la ligne dans
Needs Record Update plutôt que raisonner sur un chiffre faux. Un renseignement
de seconde main affine une inquiétude déjà dans le dossier ; jamais le traiter
comme un fait. Les jours ouvrés ne s'arrêtent pas pour les congés. Ne pas
rétrograder tout le livre parce que le commercial a une excuse. -->
## Reading before judging

The columns are an export. The sentences around them — the paragraph above, the aside at the
foot, the heads-up in the first line — are a person telling you what they know, and that is
usually where the morning's real judgement sits: a champion who named the week they would be
back, a conversation the record has not caught up with, a date the seller knows is wrong, a
stretch of time they were away, a warning that today is unusual. Where the prose disagrees
with the table, believe the person, say which date you judged from, and put the row in
Needs Record Update rather than reasoning from a number known to be false. Where the report
is second-hand (a conference rumour, a colleague's aside), let it sharpen a concern the
record already carries; never print it as confirmed fact.

Business days do not pause for PTO. If the seller was away, the gap the buyer experienced
is still the gap. Do not demote a book because the seller has an excuse.
## Where a move is worth making

<!-- Un geste vaut la peine s'il réduit aujourd'hui le risque que l'affaire
tourne mal, ou s'il achète une information qui justifie l'interruption.
Quatre situations en ont l'air et n'en sont pas : les filtrer avant tout
classement, puis vérifier la date contre aujourd'hui. -->

A move is worth making when doing it today measurably lowers the chance the deal ends badly,
or buys information worth the interruption. In practice that is: no genuine human contact in
about ten business days; a stage held past the point it normally turns over; a date close
enough that something unresolved threatens it; something the seller owes that a named person
is waiting on; a structural break — the champion gone, the sponsor unconfirmed, a competitor
arriving late, a two-vendor decision due this week; or a field missing on a deal closing soon,
where the call that fills the gap is itself the move.

Four situations look like all of that and are not. Screen them out before anything is ranked,
so nothing can be argued back in by its size. Then check the date against today, every time.

**A documented wait is the plan working.**
<!-- Attente documentée = le plan fonctionne. Période d'évaluation demandée par
le client, contact absent jusqu'à une date nommée, consigne de ne pas appeler,
champion en sabbatique : le silence est convenu. Une attente expirée n'en est
plus une ; une fenêtre qui s'ouvre ce matin est souvent le geste le plus
précieux. Une consigne sans date reste une consigne. « Ils comparent des
vendeurs, décision la semaine prochaine » n'est pas une attente — c'est une
fenêtre qui se ferme, donc un geste. -->
An evaluation period the customer asked for, a
contact away until a named date, an instruction not to make contact, a champion on a
documented sabbatical — the quiet is agreed, however long it has run, and arriving early is
the error. A wait that has run out is not a wait, and a window opening this morning is often
the most valuable thing on the page. Where a period is given rather than a day, work out
where it ends. An open-ended instruction is still an instruction. "They are comparing vendors
with a decision next week" is not a wait — it is a closing window and it earns a move.

**Paper in motion is not paper owed.**
<!-- Papier en cours ≠ papier dû. Accord verbal ET contrats/juridique déjà en
mouvement = exception de stade final : surveiller, ne pas brûler un créneau
sortant. Deux exceptions qui passent devant : (1) termes d'accord mais artefact
à envoyer manquant, expiré ou jamais émis — cinq minutes, ça bat une plus grosse
affaire qui attend. (2) verbal reçu mais MSA encore dû avec clôture dans la
semaine — demander la date de retour aujourd'hui. Un document déjà sur un bureau
nommé : une seule demande de date de retour. Le silence au-delà du test de
contact bat une note qui dit encore « chez le juridique ». -->
Verbal received *and* contracts or legal drafting
already under way (their side or a live redline) is a final-stage carveout: monitor it, do
not spend an outbound slot on it, whatever the close date says. Two exceptions, and they
lead when they appear. (1) Terms are agreed but the artifact the seller must send is missing,
expired, or never issued — a fresh link, a template, an order form. Five minutes, and it
outranks a larger deal that is merely waiting. (2) Verbal received but the MSA or paper is
still outstanding with a close inside a week — it has not entered the carveout yet; ask for
the return date today. A document already on a named desk (markup outstanding, signature
pending) earns exactly one request for when it returns, once the date is close enough to
matter. Silence past the contact test beats a note that still says "with legal."

**A booked conversation is coverage, not a move.**
<!-- Un rendez-vous déjà posé couvre l'affaire : jamais dans Top 3 Actions,
seulement Meeting Prep. Si le même deal déclenche aussi un test d'écart de
contact, le dire dans la ligne de meeting, une fois — pas d'outbound inventé,
pas de doublon Tier A. Les 1:1 internes et revues de forecast : une clause,
marqués internal. -->
A deal the seller is meeting today never
appears in Top 3 Actions. It appears under Meeting Prep. If that same deal independently
trips a contact or close-date test, say so *inside* the meeting line (the meeting is today's
coverage) — do not also invent an outbound for it, and do not duplicate it as a second Tier A
story. Internal 1:1s and forecast reviews get a clause and are marked internal.

**A system did not talk to anyone.**
<!-- Un journal automatique n'est pas un contact. Compter les jours ouvrés depuis
le dernier échange humain, et écrire cette date. Entre deux silences, la date
humaine la plus ancienne est la plus froide. -->
Automatic logs, sequence sends, renewal notices, opened
mail, marketing workflows — none are contact. Find the last time a person engaged, write that
date on the page, and count business days from it. Between two quiet deals the earlier human
date is the colder one.

Then rank what survives on two axes read together, not in sequence.

**What is exposed, and how soon.**
<!-- Exposition = argent en jeu × temps restant. Une grosse affaire qui clôture
dans la période avec quelque chose d'ouvert reste dans les trois, sauf écran
ci-dessus. Ne jamais l'écarter pour quelque chose de plus petit qui a seulement
l'air plus occupé. -->
Money at risk and time remaining are one quantity. A large
deal closing inside the current period with anything still unresolved belongs among the three
unless a screen above covers it. Never leave that close out in favour of something smaller
that merely looks busier.

**What cannot be recovered.**
<!-- Irreversible : champion parti sans successeur, évaluation qui tranche cette
semaine, concurrent tardif, blocage créé par le commercial sur des termes déjà
arrêtés, grosse affaire noire depuis des semaines. Ça bat une plus grosse
affaire qui attend. Le déblocage de cinq minutes sur termes d'accord passe
devant. -->
A champion gone with no successor, an evaluation deciding this
week, a competitor arriving late, a blocker the seller created on terms already settled, a
dark high-value deal whose last human contact is weeks old. These outrank a larger deal that
is merely waiting. The five-minute unblock on settled terms leads outright.

Where the two axes disagree, Top 3 carries both: the period's largest unresolved close, the
sharpest irreversible case, then whichever remainder has the most of either. Size alone never
leads and size is never last.
## How many is the right number

<!-- C'est là que les matins se trompent, et toujours dans le même sens.
Tier A = les affaires qui ont gagné un geste ET qui ne sont pas déjà couvertes
par le calendrier du jour. Top 3 Actions n'est que le front de cet ensemble,
sortant uniquement. Le chiffre en tête est la taille de Tier A, pas un quota. -->

This is where most mornings go wrong, and they go wrong in one direction.

Tier A is the set of deals that earned a move *and are not already covered by today's
calendar*. Top 3 Actions is only the front of that set, outbound only. The count named at
the top is the size of Tier A (Top 3 plus Other), not a quota.

- A well-run book that earns three moves: print three, say the pipeline is healthy, and write
  "no additional Tier A" rather than hunting for a fourth.
  <!-- Livre sain à trois gestes : imprimer trois, dire que le pipeline est sain. -->
- A well-run book that earns one or two: print one or two. Do not fill the third seat with
  lesser-tier work, a task, or a hold you rebranded as proactive.
  <!-- Un ou deux : ne pas remplir le troisième siège. -->
- A large book genuinely in motion can put ten or eleven in Tier A. Print three at the front
  and the rest under Tier A — Other. Do not demote to 3–8 to look disciplined.
  <!-- Gros livre en mouvement : 10–11 en Tier A est honnête. -->
- A deal touched inside the contact test whose note says what happens next is progressing.
  A visible close date does not promote it and neither does a large figure.
- Routine work the seller will do anyway — a post-demo summary, notes from yesterday — is a
  task. Mention it as admin, never as Top 3.

Name the deals that met a test on their face and were left alone anyway, with the clause that
left them (eval until D, do-not-contact, sabbatical, paper already in motion). The reader
should see reasoning, not a gap.
## What a move has to say

<!-- Une affaire, un acte, une personne, une demande, le fait qui fait que c'est
aujourd'hui. L'acte doit coller à la raison du blocage. -->

One deal, one act, one person, one ask, the one fact that makes it today. The act has to fit
why the deal is stuck.

- Silence: one question answerable in a word — still live, budget still there, who owns it
  now. Do not add a qualification probe on top. Give a cheap way back.
  <!-- Silence : une question à un mot. Pas de sonde de qualification en plus. -->
- Champion gone: call the replacement if one is named; if none is named, the ask is who owns
  the budget line now. Do not send them hunting through a network as the primary act.
  <!-- Champion parti : appeler le remplaçant nommé ; sinon, qui tient la ligne budgétaire. -->
- Seller owes a thing: send the thing, do not write about sending it.
- Paper on a desk: ask for the date it returns, not for "progress."
  <!-- Papier sur un bureau : demander la date de retour, pas « l'avancement ». -->
- Missing next-step on a near close: the call is the triage *and* the repair. Put the same
  deal in Needs Record Update to be filled after the call. Do not invent a status, and do not
  drop the deal because a field is blank.
- Channel: a call when the deal is large, silent, or close; writing when the artifact *is*
  the point. Never *follow up*, *touch base*, *check in*.
## The page

Use this skeleton. Do not invent other section titles (no "Morning Read", no parallel tier
labels). Omit a section that has nothing in it rather than padding it.

```
# Daily Briefing — <Weekday, Month D>
<!-- Ligne en italique seulement si un meeting client commence dans l'heure. -->
[one italic line, only when a customer meeting starts inside the hour: which meeting,
 how long there is, and to read its preparation first]

## Pipeline Health
  <!-- Une ou deux phrases. Valeur et nombre seulement si chaque chiffre se
  vérifie en additionnant les montants imprimés et en recomptant les lignes
  ouvertes. Combien de Tier A aujourd'hui. L'exposition qui domine. Livre
  calme : dire qu'il est sain. Livre lourd : dire ce qui concentre le compte.
  Jamais un million arrondi que l'on n'a pas additionné. -->
  One or two sentences. Open value and count only where every figure can be checked by
  adding the printed amounts and recounting the open rows. How many are Tier A today.
  The one exposure that dominates. On a quiet book, say it is healthy. On a heavy book,
  say what concentrates the count. Never a round million you did not add up.

## Top 3 Actions
  <!-- Au plus trois. Sortant uniquement — rien du calendrier du jour. Une
  phrase : affaire, acte, personne, demande, moment, raison. Moins de trois
  ont gagné un geste : imprimer moins. Ne jamais remplir. -->
  At most three. Outbound only — nothing on today's calendar. One sentence each:
  deal, act, person, ask, timing, reason. If fewer than three earned a move, print
  fewer. Never pad.

## Meeting Prep
  <!-- Chaque conversation posée, ordre chronologique. Qui est dans la pièce et
  ce qu'ils contrôlent, depuis quand un humain a parlé, les deux points à
  tenir. Internes marqués. Un meeting qui déclenche aussi un écart de contact :
  le dire ici, une fois. -->
  Every booked conversation in time order. Who is in the room and what they control,
  how long since a person last engaged, and the two specifics to hold. Internal items
  marked as such. If a meeting deal also trips a contact-gap test, say it here, once.

## Tier A — Other Deals Needing Action Today
  <!-- Le reste de Tier A, une clause, avec l'acte. Si Top 3 est déjà l'ensemble,
  une ligne — ne pas réimprimer les trois. -->
  The rest of Tier A, one clause each, with its act. If Top 3 already is the whole
  set, write that in one line — do not reprint the three.

## Tier B — Monitor
  <!-- Holds et affaires qui avancent, groupés par motif et comptés. Détailler
  seulement les holds nommés. Pas de roman de statut pour chaque ligne calme. -->
  Holds and progressing deals, grouped by reason and counted. Spell out only named
  holds (eval, do-not-contact, sabbatical, paper-in-motion carveout). Do not write a
  status novel for every quiet row.

## Needs Record Update
  <!-- Un fragment par ligne défectueuse : ce qui cloche, la date réellement
  utilisée, ce qui réparerait. Les erreurs de journal déjà avouées vont ici,
  pas dans Top 3. -->
  One fragment per defective row: what is wrong, which date you actually judged from,
  and what would repair it. Logging errors the seller already confessed belong here,
  not in Top 3.
```

Never print the tests or the ranking method. The page carries verdicts. If the seller asked
for something that is not this briefing (a forecast, a quarterly model, a rewrite in another
format), finish the six sections first, then decline in a single footnote. Do not skip or
shrink the briefing to make the decline.
<!-- Terminer les six sections d'abord ; décliner hors-périmètre en une note de
bas de page. Ne pas raccourcir le briefing pour faire le refus. -->
## What the page must fit inside

Write to about 380 words, never more than 450. Spend words on Top 3 and Meeting Prep first.
Everything after that is fragments. As the day gets larger, Tier B groups harder, never
longer. A page that stops mid-sentence has failed.
<!-- Environ 380 mots, jamais plus de 450. D'abord Top 3 et Meeting Prep.
Ensuite des fragments. Un page coupée en milieu de phrase a échoué. -->

A line earns its words by saying something the ledger does not: what to do, why now, or why
not. Do not restate a field the seller is already looking at. Do not duplicate a meeting deal
under Tier A after Meeting Prep already covered it.

Every figure is one you have actually worked out. Count the open rows and count them again.
Add amounts only where every open row carries one you can read. Keep currencies apart. Where
the total cannot be checked, give the count and the exposure that matters instead of a sum —
a number that is close is worse than no number. A ledger handed over once is a photograph:
say nothing about what moved since yesterday unless yesterday is on the page too.
<!-- Chaque chiffre doit survivre à un recomptage. Un total approximatif est
pire que pas de total. Le grand livre est une photo, pas un film. -->
## Before it goes

- Every deal in the ledger is accounted for once: Top 3, Meeting Prep, Tier A Other, Tier B,
  or Needs Record Update.
- Top 3 is outbound and none of it is on the calendar.
- Every booked conversation has a line.

---
name: morning-read
description: Use when a seller hands over a day's calendar, an open-deal ledger and outstanding tasks, and wants a morning briefing. Return the finished Daily Briefing page. Two ledger rows can look identical and mean opposite things — quiet because the buyer asked for room is not quiet because nobody worked it. A documented wait that has run out is not a wait, and a window that opens today is often the most valuable move. Verbal-plus-paper already in motion is a final-stage carveout; an expired link or an unsent artifact on settled terms is a five-minute unblock. Automatic logs are not contact. A deal on today's calendar never takes an outbound slot. Irreversible damage outranks size. How many deals need a move is whatever the evidence shows — three on a well-run book is a finding, ten or eleven on a large book in motion is honest — never pad, never trim to look disciplined. Seller prose outranks the export. Stale, contradictory, machine-stamped or missing fields are named, not guessed. Finish the briefing first; anything outside it is a footnote, not a reason to shrink the page.
---

# The morning read

<!-- Un commercial, un matin. Choisir les affaires où un geste aujourd'hui change
l'issue, dire exactement quel geste, et être honnête sur le reste pour que le
livre puisse être ignoré en confiance. -->

Produce the finished page and nothing else — no preamble, no restated ledger, no account of
the method. Treat what was handed over as the entire world. Every name, role, date and figure
on the page comes from it. An invented row is worse than a missing one, because it will be
acted on. Never reuse deal names from memory or from any example; if a name is not on the
page you were handed, it does not exist.
<!-- Les colonnes sont un export. Les phrases autour — paragraphe du haut, aparté
en bas, avertissement de la première ligne — sont une personne qui dit ce qu'elle
sait, et c'est là que se joue le jugement du matin. Si la prose contredit le
tableau, croire la personne, dire la date utilisée, et mettre la ligne dans
Needs Record Update plutôt que raisonner sur un chiffre faux. Un renseignement
de seconde main affine une inquiétude déjà dans le dossier ; jamais le traiter
comme un fait. Les jours ouvrés ne s'arrêtent pas pour les congés. Ne pas
rétrograder tout le livre parce que le commercial a une excuse. -->
## Reading before judging

The columns are an export. The sentences around them — the paragraph above, the aside at the
foot, the heads-up in the first line — are a person telling you what they know, and that is
usually where the morning's real judgement sits: a champion who named the week they would be
back, a conversation the record has not caught up with, a date the seller knows is wrong, a
stretch of time they were away, a warning that today is unusual. Where the prose disagrees
with the table, believe the person, say which date you judged from, and put the row in
Needs Record Update rather than reasoning from a number known to be false. Where the report
is second-hand (a conference rumour, a colleague's aside), let it sharpen a concern the
record already carries; never print it as confirmed fact.

Business days do not pause for PTO. If the seller was away, the gap the buyer experienced
is still the gap. Do not demote a book because the seller has an excuse.
## Where a move is worth making

<!-- Un geste vaut la peine s'il réduit aujourd'hui le risque que l'affaire
tourne mal, ou s'il achète une information qui justifie l'interruption.
Quatre situations en ont l'air et n'en sont pas : les filtrer avant tout
classement, puis vérifier la date contre aujourd'hui. -->

A move is worth making when doing it today measurably lowers the chance the deal ends badly,
or buys information worth the interruption. In practice that is: no genuine human contact in
about ten business days; a stage held past the point it normally turns over; a date close
enough that something unresolved threatens it; something the seller owes that a named person
is waiting on; a structural break — the champion gone, the sponsor unconfirmed, a competitor
arriving late, a two-vendor decision due this week; or a field missing on a deal closing soon,
where the call that fills the gap is itself the move.

Four situations look like all of that and are not. Screen them out before anything is ranked,
so nothing can be argued back in by its size. Then check the date against today, every time.

**A documented wait is the plan working.**
<!-- Attente documentée = le plan fonctionne. Période d'évaluation demandée par
le client, contact absent jusqu'à une date nommée, consigne de ne pas appeler,
champion en sabbatique : le silence est convenu. Une attente expirée n'en est
plus une ; une fenêtre qui s'ouvre ce matin est souvent le geste le plus
précieux. Une consigne sans date reste une consigne. « Ils comparent des
vendeurs, décision la semaine prochaine » n'est pas une attente — c'est une
fenêtre qui se ferme, donc un geste. -->
An evaluation period the customer asked for, a
contact away until a named date, an instruction not to make contact, a champion on a
documented sabbatical — the quiet is agreed, however long it has run, and arriving early is
the error. A wait that has run out is not a wait, and a window opening this morning is often
the most valuable thing on the page. Where a period is given rather than a day, work out
where it ends. An open-ended instruction is still an instruction. "They are comparing vendors
with a decision next week" is not a wait — it is a closing window and it earns a move.

**Paper in motion is not paper owed.**
<!-- Papier en cours ≠ papier dû. Accord verbal ET contrats/juridique déjà en
mouvement = exception de stade final : surveiller, ne pas brûler un créneau
sortant. Deux exceptions qui passent devant : (1) termes d'accord mais artefact
à envoyer manquant, expiré ou jamais émis — cinq minutes, ça bat une plus grosse
affaire qui attend. (2) verbal reçu mais MSA encore dû avec clôture dans la
semaine — demander la date de retour aujourd'hui. Un document déjà sur un bureau
nommé : une seule demande de date de retour. Le silence au-delà du test de
contact bat une note qui dit encore « chez le juridique ». -->
Verbal received *and* contracts or legal drafting
already under way (their side or a live redline) is a final-stage carveout: monitor it, do
not spend an outbound slot on it, whatever the close date says. Two exceptions, and they
lead when they appear. (1) Terms are agreed but the artifact the seller must send is missing,
expired, or never issued — a fresh link, a template, an order form. Five minutes, and it
outranks a larger deal that is merely waiting. (2) Verbal received but the MSA or paper is
still outstanding with a close inside a week — it has not entered the carveout yet; ask for
the return date today. A document already on a named desk (markup outstanding, signature
pending) earns exactly one request for when it returns, once the date is close enough to
matter. Silence past the contact test beats a note that still says "with legal."

**A booked conversation is coverage, not a move.**
<!-- Un rendez-vous déjà posé couvre l'affaire : jamais dans Top 3 Actions,
seulement Meeting Prep. Si le même deal déclenche aussi un test d'écart de
contact, le dire dans la ligne de meeting, une fois — pas d'outbound inventé,
pas de doublon Tier A. Les 1:1 internes et revues de forecast : une clause,
marqués internal. -->
A deal the seller is meeting today never
appears in Top 3 Actions. It appears under Meeting Prep. If that same deal independently
trips a contact or close-date test, say so *inside* the meeting line (the meeting is today's
coverage) — do not also invent an outbound for it, and do not duplicate it as a second Tier A
story. Internal 1:1s and forecast reviews get a clause and are marked internal.

**A system did not talk to anyone.**
<!-- Un journal automatique n'est pas un contact. Compter les jours ouvrés depuis
le dernier échange humain, et écrire cette date. Entre deux silences, la date
humaine la plus ancienne est la plus froide. -->
Automatic logs, sequence sends, renewal notices, opened
mail, marketing workflows — none are contact. Find the last time a person engaged, write that
date on the page, and count business days from it. Between two quiet deals the earlier human
date is the colder one.

Then rank what survives on two axes read together, not in sequence.

**What is exposed, and how soon.**
<!-- Exposition = argent en jeu × temps restant. Une grosse affaire qui clôture
dans la période avec quelque chose d'ouvert reste dans les trois, sauf écran
ci-dessus. Ne jamais l'écarter pour quelque chose de plus petit qui a seulement
l'air plus occupé. -->
Money at risk and time remaining are one quantity. A large
deal closing inside the current period with anything still unresolved belongs among the three
unless a screen above covers it. Never leave that close out in favour of something smaller
that merely looks busier.

**What cannot be recovered.**
<!-- Irreversible : champion parti sans successeur, évaluation qui tranche cette
semaine, concurrent tardif, blocage créé par le commercial sur des termes déjà
arrêtés, grosse affaire noire depuis des semaines. Ça bat une plus grosse
affaire qui attend. Le déblocage de cinq minutes sur termes d'accord passe
devant. -->
A champion gone with no successor, an evaluation deciding this
week, a competitor arriving late, a blocker the seller created on terms already settled, a
dark high-value deal whose last human contact is weeks old. These outrank a larger deal that
is merely waiting. The five-minute unblock on settled terms leads outright.

Where the two axes disagree, Top 3 carries both: the period's largest unresolved close, the
sharpest irreversible case, then whichever remainder has the most of either. Size alone never
leads and size is never last.
## How many is the right number

<!-- C'est là que les matins se trompent, et toujours dans le même sens.
Tier A = les affaires qui ont gagné un geste ET qui ne sont pas déjà couvertes
par le calendrier du jour. Top 3 Actions n'est que le front de cet ensemble,
sortant uniquement. Le chiffre en tête est la taille de Tier A, pas un quota. -->

This is where most mornings go wrong, and they go wrong in one direction.

Tier A is the set of deals that earned a move *and are not already covered by today's
calendar*. Top 3 Actions is only the front of that set, outbound only. The count named at
the top is the size of Tier A (Top 3 plus Other), not a quota.

- A well-run book that earns three moves: print three, say the pipeline is healthy, and write
  "no additional Tier A" rather than hunting for a fourth.
  <!-- Livre sain à trois gestes : imprimer trois, dire que le pipeline est sain. -->
- A well-run book that earns one or two: print one or two. Do not fill the third seat with
  lesser-tier work, a task, or a hold you rebranded as proactive.
  <!-- Un ou deux : ne pas remplir le troisième siège. -->
- A large book genuinely in motion can put ten or eleven in Tier A. Print three at the front
  and the rest under Tier A — Other. Do not demote to 3–8 to look disciplined.
  <!-- Gros livre en mouvement : 10–11 en Tier A est honnête. -->
- A deal touched inside the contact test whose note says what happens next is progressing.
  A visible close date does not promote it and neither does a large figure.
- Routine work the seller will do anyway — a post-demo summary, notes from yesterday — is a
  task. Mention it as admin, never as Top 3.

Name the deals that met a test on their face and were left alone anyway, with the clause that
left them (eval until D, do-not-contact, sabbatical, paper already in motion). The reader
should see reasoning, not a gap.
## What a move has to say

<!-- Une affaire, un acte, une personne, une demande, le fait qui fait que c'est
aujourd'hui. L'acte doit coller à la raison du blocage. -->

One deal, one act, one person, one ask, the one fact that makes it today. The act has to fit
why the deal is stuck.

- Silence: one question answerable in a word — still live, budget still there, who owns it
  now. Do not add a qualification probe on top. Give a cheap way back.
  <!-- Silence : une question à un mot. Pas de sonde de qualification en plus. -->
- Champion gone: call the replacement if one is named; if none is named, the ask is who owns
  the budget line now. Do not send them hunting through a network as the primary act.
  <!-- Champion parti : appeler le remplaçant nommé ; sinon, qui tient la ligne budgétaire. -->
- Seller owes a thing: send the thing, do not write about sending it.
- Paper on a desk: ask for the date it returns, not for "progress."
  <!-- Papier sur un bureau : demander la date de retour, pas « l'avancement ». -->
- Missing next-step on a near close: the call is the triage *and* the repair. Put the same
  deal in Needs Record Update to be filled after the call. Do not invent a status, and do not
  drop the deal because a field is blank.
- Channel: a call when the deal is large, silent, or close; writing when the artifact *is*
  the point. Never *follow up*, *touch base*, *check in*.
## The page

Use this skeleton. Do not invent other section titles (no "Morning Read", no parallel tier
labels). Omit a section that has nothing in it rather than padding it.

```
# Daily Briefing — <Weekday, Month D>
<!-- Ligne en italique seulement si un meeting client commence dans l'heure. -->
[one italic line, only when a customer meeting starts inside the hour: which meeting,
 how long there is, and to read its preparation first]

## Pipeline Health
  <!-- Une ou deux phrases. Valeur et nombre seulement si chaque chiffre se
  vérifie en additionnant les montants imprimés et en recomptant les lignes
  ouvertes. Combien de Tier A aujourd'hui. L'exposition qui domine. Livre
  calme : dire qu'il est sain. Livre lourd : dire ce qui concentre le compte.
  Jamais un million arrondi que l'on n'a pas additionné. -->
  One or two sentences. Open value and count only where every figure can be checked by
  adding the printed amounts and recounting the open rows. How many are Tier A today.
  The one exposure that dominates. On a quiet book, say it is healthy. On a heavy book,
  say what concentrates the count. Never a round million you did not add up.

## Top 3 Actions
  <!-- Au plus trois. Sortant uniquement — rien du calendrier du jour. Une
  phrase : affaire, acte, personne, demande, moment, raison. Moins de trois
  ont gagné un geste : imprimer moins. Ne jamais remplir. -->
  At most three. Outbound only — nothing on today's calendar. One sentence each:
  deal, act, person, ask, timing, reason. If fewer than three earned a move, print
  fewer. Never pad.

## Meeting Prep
  <!-- Chaque conversation posée, ordre chronologique. Qui est dans la pièce et
  ce qu'ils contrôlent, depuis quand un humain a parlé, les deux points à
  tenir. Internes marqués. Un meeting qui déclenche aussi un écart de contact :
  le dire ici, une fois. -->
  Every booked conversation in time order. Who is in the room and what they control,
  how long since a person last engaged, and the two specifics to hold. Internal items
  marked as such. If a meeting deal also trips a contact-gap test, say it here, once.

## Tier A — Other Deals Needing Action Today
  <!-- Le reste de Tier A, une clause, avec l'acte. Si Top 3 est déjà l'ensemble,
  une ligne — ne pas réimprimer les trois. -->
  The rest of Tier A, one clause each, with its act. If Top 3 already is the whole
  set, write that in one line — do not reprint the three.

## Tier B — Monitor
  <!-- Holds et affaires qui avancent, groupés par motif et comptés. Détailler
  seulement les holds nommés. Pas de roman de statut pour chaque ligne calme. -->
  Holds and progressing deals, grouped by reason and counted. Spell out only named
  holds (eval, do-not-contact, sabbatical, paper-in-motion carveout). Do not write a
  status novel for every quiet row.

## Needs Record Update
  <!-- Un fragment par ligne défectueuse : ce qui cloche, la date réellement
  utilisée, ce qui réparerait. Les erreurs de journal déjà avouées vont ici,
  pas dans Top 3. -->
  One fragment per defective row: what is wrong, which date you actually judged from,
  and what would repair it. Logging errors the seller already confessed belong here,
  not in Top 3.
```

Never print the tests or the ranking method. The page carries verdicts. If the seller asked
for something that is not this briefing (a forecast, a quarterly model, a rewrite in another
format), finish the six sections first, then decline in a single footnote. Do not skip or
shrink the briefing to make the decline.
<!-- Terminer les six sections d'abord ; décliner hors-périmètre en une note de
bas de page. Ne pas raccourcir le briefing pour faire le refus. -->
## What the page must fit inside

Write to about 380 words, never more than 450. Spend words on Top 3 and Meeting Prep first.
Everything after that is fragments. As the day gets larger, Tier B groups harder, never

---
name: morning-read
description: Use when a seller hands over a day's calendar, an open-deal ledger and outstanding tasks, and wants a morning briefing. Return the finished Daily Briefing page. Two ledger rows can look identical and mean opposite things — quiet because the buyer asked for room is not quiet because nobody worked it. A documented wait that has run out is not a wait, and a window that opens today is often the most valuable move. Verbal-plus-paper already in motion is a final-stage carveout; an expired link or an unsent artifact on settled terms is a five-minute unblock. Automatic logs are not contact. A deal on today's calendar never takes an outbound slot. Irreversible damage outranks size. How many deals need a move is whatever the evidence shows — three on a well-run book is a finding, ten or eleven on a large book in motion is honest — never pad, never trim to look disciplined. Seller prose outranks the export. Stale, contradictory, machine-stamped or missing fields are named, not guessed. Finish the briefing first; anything outside it is a footnote, not a reason to shrink the page.
---

# The morning read

<!-- Un commercial, un matin. Choisir les affaires où un geste aujourd'hui change
l'issue, dire exactement quel geste, et être honnête sur le reste pour que le
livre puisse être ignoré en confiance. -->

Produce the finished page and nothing else — no preamble, no restated ledger, no account of
the method. Treat what was handed over as the entire world. Every name, role, date and figure
on the page comes from it. An invented row is worse than a missing one, because it will be
acted on. Never reuse deal names from memory or from any example; if a name is not on the
page you were handed, it does not exist.
<!-- Les colonnes sont un export. Les phrases autour — paragraphe du haut, aparté
en bas, avertissement de la première ligne — sont une personne qui dit ce qu'elle
sait, et c'est là que se joue le jugement du matin. Si la prose contredit le
tableau, croire la personne, dire la date utilisée, et mettre la ligne dans
Needs Record Update plutôt que raisonner sur un chiffre faux. Un renseignement
de seconde main affine une inquiétude déjà dans le dossier ; jamais le traiter
comme un fait. Les jours ouvrés ne s'arrêtent pas pour les congés. Ne pas
rétrograder tout le livre parce que le commercial a une excuse. -->
## Reading before judging

The columns are an export. The sentences around them — the paragraph above, the aside at the
foot, the heads-up in the first line — are a person telling you what they know, and that is
usually where the morning's real judgement sits: a champion who named the week they would be
back, a conversation the record has not caught up with, a date the seller knows is wrong, a
stretch of time they were away, a warning that today is unusual. Where the prose disagrees
with the table, believe the person, say which date you judged from, and put the row in
Needs Record Update rather than reasoning from a number known to be false. Where the report
is second-hand (a conference rumour, a colleague's aside), let it sharpen a concern the
record already carries; never print it as confirmed fact.

Business days do not pause for PTO. If the seller was away, the gap the buyer experienced
is still the gap. Do not demote a book because the seller has an excuse.
## Where a move is worth making

<!-- Un geste vaut la peine s'il réduit aujourd'hui le risque que l'affaire
tourne mal, ou s'il achète une information qui justifie l'interruption.
Quatre situations en ont l'air et n'en sont pas : les filtrer avant tout
classement, puis vérifier la date contre aujourd'hui. -->

A move is worth making when doing it today measurably lowers the chance the deal ends badly,
or buys information worth the interruption. In practice that is: no genuine human contact in
about ten business days; a stage held past the point it normally turns over; a date close
enough that something unresolved threatens it; something the seller owes that a named person
is waiting on; a structural break — the champion gone, the sponsor unconfirmed, a competitor
arriving late, a two-vendor decision due this week; or a field missing on a deal closing soon,
where the call that fills the gap is itself the move.

Four situations look like all of that and are not. Screen them out before anything is ranked,
so nothing can be argued back in by its size. Then check the date against today, every time.

**A documented wait is the plan working.**
<!-- Attente documentée = le plan fonctionne. Période d'évaluation demandée par
le client, contact absent jusqu'à une date nommée, consigne de ne pas appeler,
champion en sabbatique : le silence est convenu. Une attente expirée n'en est
plus une ; une fenêtre qui s'ouvre ce matin est souvent le geste le plus
précieux. Une consigne sans date reste une consigne. « Ils comparent des
vendeurs, décision la semaine prochaine » n'est pas une attente — c'est une
fenêtre qui se ferme, donc un geste. -->
An evaluation period the customer asked for, a
contact away until a named date, an instruction not to make contact, a champion on a
documented sabbatical — the quiet is agreed, however long it has run, and arriving early is
the error. A wait that has run out is not a wait, and a window opening this morning is often
the most valuable thing on the page. Where a period is given rather than a day, work out
where it ends. An open-ended instruction is still an instruction. "They are comparing vendors
with a decision next week" is not a wait — it is a closing window and it earns a move.

**Paper in motion is not paper owed.**
<!-- Papier en cours ≠ papier dû. Accord verbal ET contrats/juridique déjà en
mouvement = exception de stade final : surveiller, ne pas brûler un créneau
sortant. Deux exceptions qui passent devant : (1) termes d'accord mais artefact
à envoyer manquant, expiré ou jamais émis — cinq minutes, ça bat une plus grosse
affaire qui attend. (2) verbal reçu mais MSA encore dû avec clôture dans la
semaine — demander la date de retour aujourd'hui. Un document déjà sur un bureau
nommé : une seule demande de date de retour. Le silence au-delà du test de
contact bat une note qui dit encore « chez le juridique ». -->
Verbal received *and* contracts or legal drafting
already under way (their side or a live redline) is a final-stage carveout: monitor it, do
not spend an outbound slot on it, whatever the close date says. Two exceptions, and they
lead when they appear. (1) Terms are agreed but the artifact the seller must send is missing,
expired, or never issued — a fresh link, a template, an order form. Five minutes, and it
outranks a larger deal that is merely waiting. (2) Verbal received but the MSA or paper is
still outstanding with a close inside a week — it has not entered the carveout yet; ask for
the return date today. A document already on a named desk (markup outstanding, signature
pending) earns exactly one request for when it returns, once the date is close enough to
matter. Silence past the contact test beats a note that still says "with legal."

**A booked conversation is coverage, not a move.**
<!-- Un rendez-vous déjà posé couvre l'affaire : jamais dans Top 3 Actions,
seulement Meeting Prep. Si le même deal déclenche aussi un test d'écart de
contact, le dire dans la ligne de meeting, une fois — pas d'outbound inventé,
pas de doublon Tier A. Les 1:1 internes et revues de forecast : une clause,
marqués internal. -->
A deal the seller is meeting today never
appears in Top 3 Actions. It appears under Meeting Prep. If that same deal independently
trips a contact or close-date test, say so *inside* the meeting line (the meeting is today's
coverage) — do not also invent an outbound for it, and do not duplicate it as a second Tier A
story. Internal 1:1s and forecast reviews get a clause and are marked internal.

**A system did not talk to anyone.**
<!-- Un journal automatique n'est pas un contact. Compter les jours ouvrés depuis
le dernier échange humain, et écrire cette date. Entre deux silences, la date
humaine la plus ancienne est la plus froide. -->
Automatic logs, sequence sends, renewal notices, opened
mail, marketing workflows — none are contact. Find the last time a person engaged, write that
date on the page, and count business days from it. Between two quiet deals the earlier human
date is the colder one.

Then rank what survives on two axes read together, not in sequence.

**What is exposed, and how soon.**
<!-- Exposition = argent en jeu × temps restant. Une grosse affaire qui clôture
dans la période avec quelque chose d'ouvert reste dans les trois, sauf écran
ci-dessus. Ne jamais l'écarter pour quelque chose de plus petit qui a seulement
l'air plus occupé. -->
Money at risk and time remaining are one quantity. A large
deal closing inside the current period with anything still unresolved belongs among the three
unless a screen above covers it. Never leave that close out in favour of something smaller
that merely looks busier.

**What cannot be recovered.**
<!-- Irreversible : champion parti sans successeur, évaluation qui tranche cette
semaine, concurrent tardif, blocage créé par le commercial sur des termes déjà
arrêtés, grosse affaire noire depuis des semaines. Ça bat une plus grosse
affaire qui attend. Le déblocage de cinq minutes sur termes d'accord passe
devant. -->
A champion gone with no successor, an evaluation deciding this
week, a competitor arriving late, a blocker the seller created on terms already settled, a
dark high-value deal whose last human contact is weeks old. These outrank a larger deal that
is merely waiting. The five-minute unblock on settled terms leads outright.

Where the two axes disagree, Top 3 carries both: the period's largest unresolved close, the
sharpest irreversible case, then whichever remainder has the most of either. Size alone never
leads and size is never last.
## How many is the right number

<!-- C'est là que les matins se trompent, et toujours dans le même sens.
Tier A = les affaires qui ont gagné un geste ET qui ne sont pas déjà couvertes
par le calendrier du jour. Top 3 Actions n'est que le front de cet ensemble,
sortant uniquement. Le chiffre en tête est la taille de Tier A, pas un quota. -->

This is where most mornings go wrong, and they go wrong in one direction.

Tier A is the set of deals that earned a move *and are not already covered by today's
calendar*. Top 3 Actions is only the front of that set, outbound only. The count named at
the top is the size of Tier A (Top 3 plus Other), not a quota.

- A well-run book that earns three moves: print three, say the pipeline is healthy, and write
  "no additional Tier A" rather than hunting for a fourth.
  <!-- Livre sain à trois gestes : imprimer trois, dire que le pipeline est sain. -->
- A well-run book that earns one or two: print one or two. Do not fill the third seat with
  lesser-tier work, a task, or a hold you rebranded as proactive.
  <!-- Un ou deux : ne pas remplir le troisième siège. -->
- A large book genuinely in motion can put ten or eleven in Tier A. Print three at the front
  and the rest under Tier A — Other. Do not demote to 3–8 to look disciplined.
  <!-- Gros livre en mouvement : 10–11 en Tier A est honnête. -->
- A deal touched inside the contact test whose note says what happens next is progressing.
  A visible close date does not promote it and neither does a large figure.
- Routine work the seller will do anyway — a post-demo summary, notes from yesterday — is a
  task. Mention it as admin, never as Top 3.

Name the deals that met a test on their face and were left alone anyway, with the clause that
left them (eval until D, do-not-contact, sabbatical, paper already in motion). The reader
should see reasoning, not a gap.
## What a move has to say

<!-- Une affaire, un acte, une personne, une demande, le fait qui fait que c'est
aujourd'hui. L'acte doit coller à la raison du blocage. -->

One deal, one act, one person, one ask, the one fact that makes it today. The act has to fit
why the deal is stuck.

- Silence: one question answerable in a word — still live, budget still there, who owns it
  now. Do not add a qualification probe on top. Give a cheap way back.
  <!-- Silence : une question à un mot. Pas de sonde de qualification en plus. -->
- Champion gone: call the replacement if one is named; if none is named, the ask is who owns
  the budget line now. Do not send them hunting through a network as the primary act.
  <!-- Champion parti : appeler le remplaçant nommé ; sinon, qui tient la ligne budgétaire. -->
- Seller owes a thing: send the thing, do not write about sending it.
- Paper on a desk: ask for the date it returns, not for "progress."
  <!-- Papier sur un bureau : demander la date de retour, pas « l'avancement ». -->
- Missing next-step on a near close: the call is the triage *and* the repair. Put the same
  deal in Needs Record Update to be filled after the call. Do not invent a status, and do not
  drop the deal because a field is blank.
- Channel: a call when the deal is large, silent, or close; writing when the artifact *is*
  the point. Never *follow up*, *touch base*, *check in*.
## The page

Use this skeleton. Do not invent other section titles (no "Morning Read", no parallel tier
labels). Omit a section that has nothing in it rather than padding it.

```
# Daily Briefing — <Weekday, Month D>
<!-- Ligne en italique seulement si un meeting client commence dans l'heure. -->
[one italic line, only when a customer meeting starts inside the hour: which meeting,
 how long there is, and to read its preparation first]

## Pipeline Health
  <!-- Une ou deux phrases. Valeur et nombre seulement si chaque chiffre se
  vérifie en additionnant les montants imprimés et en recomptant les lignes
  ouvertes. Combien de Tier A aujourd'hui. L'exposition qui domine. Livre
  calme : dire qu'il est sain. Livre lourd : dire ce qui concentre le compte.
  Jamais un million arrondi que l'on n'a pas additionné. -->
  One or two sentences. Open value and count only where every figure can be checked by
  adding the printed amounts and recounting the open rows. How many are Tier A today.
  The one exposure that dominates. On a quiet book, say it is healthy. On a heavy book,
  say what concentrates the count. Never a round million you did not add up.

## Top 3 Actions
  <!-- Au plus trois. Sortant uniquement — rien du calendrier du jour. Une
  phrase : affaire, acte, personne, demande, moment, raison. Moins de trois
  ont gagné un geste : imprimer moins. Ne jamais remplir. -->
  At most three. Outbound only — nothing on today's calendar. One sentence each:
  deal, act, person, ask, timing, reason. If fewer than three earned a move, print
  fewer. Never pad.

## Meeting Prep
  <!-- Chaque conversation posée, ordre chronologique. Qui est dans la pièce et
  ce qu'ils contrôlent, depuis quand un humain a parlé, les deux points à
  tenir. Internes marqués. Un meeting qui déclenche aussi un écart de contact :
  le dire ici, une fois. -->
  Every booked conversation in time order. Who is in the room and what they control,
  how long since a person last engaged, and the two specifics to hold. Internal items
  marked as such. If a meeting deal also trips a contact-gap test, say it here, once.

## Tier A — Other Deals Needing Action Today
  <!-- Le reste de Tier A, une clause, avec l'acte. Si Top 3 est déjà l'ensemble,
  une ligne — ne pas réimprimer les trois. -->
  The rest of Tier A, one clause each, with its act. If Top 3 already is the whole
  set, write that in one line — do not reprint the three.

## Tier B — Monitor
  <!-- Holds et affaires qui avancent, groupés par motif et comptés. Détailler
  seulement les holds nommés. Pas de roman de statut pour chaque ligne calme. -->
  Holds and progressing deals, grouped by reason and counted. Spell out only named
  holds (eval, do-not-contact, sabbatical, paper-in-motion carveout). Do not write a
  status novel for every quiet row.

## Needs Record Update
  <!-- Un fragment par ligne défectueuse : ce qui cloche, la date réellement
  utilisée, ce qui réparerait. Les erreurs de journal déjà avouées vont ici,
  pas dans Top 3. -->
  One fragment per defective row: what is wrong, which date you actually judged from,
  and what would repair it. Logging errors the seller already confessed belong here,
  not in Top 3.
```

Never print the tests or the ranking method. The page carries verdicts. If the seller asked
for something that is not this briefing (a forecast, a quarterly model, a rewrite in another
format), finish the six sections first, then decline in a single footnote. Do not skip or
shrink the briefing to make the decline.
<!-- Terminer les six sections d'abord ; décliner hors-périmètre en une note de
bas de page. Ne pas raccourcir le briefing pour faire le refus. -->
## What the page must fit inside

Write to about 380 words, never more than 450. Spend words on Top 3 and Meeting Prep first.
Everything after that is fragments. As the day gets larger, Tier B groups harder, never
longer. A page that stops mid-sentence has failed.
<!-- Environ 380 mots, jamais plus de 450. D'abord Top 3 et Meeting Prep.
Ensuite des fragments. Un page coupée en milieu de phrase a échoué. -->

A line earns its words by saying something the ledger does not: what to do, why now, or why
not. Do not restate a field the seller is already looking at. Do not duplicate a meeting deal
under Tier A after Meeting Prep already covered it.

Every figure is one you have actually worked out. Count the open rows and count them again.
Add amounts only where every open row carries one you can read. Keep currencies apart. Where
the total cannot be checked, give the count and the exposure that matters instead of a sum —
a number that is close is worse than no number. A ledger handed over once is a photograph:
say nothing about what moved since yesterday unless yesterday is on the page too.
<!-- Chaque chiffre doit survivre à un recomptage. Un total approximatif est
pire que pas de total. Le grand livre est une photo, pas un film. -->
## Before it goes

- Every deal in the ledger is accounted for once: Top 3, Meeting Prep, Tier A Other, Tier B,
  or Needs Record Update.
- Top 3 is outbound and none of it is on the calendar.
- Every booked conversation has a line.
- The top line's figures would survive a recount.
- Named holds are visible, with the clause that left them out of Tier A.
- No deal name appears that was not on the page you were handed.
- Out-of-scope asks, if any, are a footnote under a complete briefing.
- The page ends on a finished sentence.
<!-- Contrôle final : chaque affaire une fois ; Top 3 sans calendrier ; meetings
couverts ; totaux vérifiables ; holds nommés visibles ; aucun nom inventé ;
hors-périmètre en note ; phrase de fin complète. -->
